requirements: Dual-currency accounting: every claimed saving must state which currency it reduces — input/prefill tokens, output/generation tokens (≈ number of calls or turns), $-per-token (via model choice), or 'safety only, no cost effect' — because these behave independently and a mechanism can cut one while raising another (e.g. injected skill specs raise input tokens while cutting output turns).

Per-instance measurability against a counterfactual: cost and reliability gains must be demonstrable on a SINGLE task instance by comparing the mechanism on vs. off on that same instance, not only as an average over a benchmark/workload distribution — this is what rules out hand-waving on tasks done once or twice, since there is no distribution to average over.

Cold-start / rare-task yield: the mechanism must produce a measurable benefit — in cost, reliability, or both — the first, second, or third time a hard task type is ever encountered, without requiring a pre-existing corpus of similar prior traces to mine, cache, or calibrate against. At worst it must be a no-op on a genuinely novel task, never negative ROI.

Authority-independent verification: the check that approves or blocks a proposed action must derive its authority from something other than the same generative process that proposed the action — a separately specified policy, an external tool or solver, deterministic code, or a human — not the acting model grading its own output. No self-certification.

Compaction/context-durability invariance: the constraint or policy a check enforces must live and be evaluable somewhere NOT subject to transcript summarization/truncation — it must not depend on the live context window still containing it, since old turns (and the policy in them) are exactly what compaction drops first.

Pre-execution, fail-closed gating: verification must happen BEFORE a side-effecting action executes (shell command, file edit, tool call, browser action, purchase, send), and when the check cannot be evaluated with confidence — a novel action shape, an ambiguous risk — the default must be refusal or escalation, not silent execution, because a rare task has no held-out failure history to have already caught the bad case.

No correctness regression: the mechanism must not lower task success rate relative to an unassisted-agent baseline; ideally it raises reliability (e.g. by catching errors before they execute) even while cutting cost — cost and correctness are both scored, not cost alone.

Overhead-bounded, self-gating cost: the mechanism's own resource use (extra calls, extra context, solver/verifier time) must be smaller than what it saves on the instance it is applied to, and the system must be able to cheaply skip its heavier machinery when an action is manifestly low-risk and low-cost to begin with.

Composability and small-team buildability: the design must layer onto existing cost levers (prompt caching, sub-agent isolation, RAG, model routing/cascades) as an orthogonal axis rather than replacing them, and must be implementable by a small team on off-the-shelf LLM APIs plus lightweight auxiliary components (static analyzers, solvers, sandboxes, transactional storage) — no bespoke foundation-model training required.

designSpace.idea: Don't re-pay prefill cost for information the model already produced or holds elsewhere: cache stable prompt/tool-schema prefixes, or treat the whole context window as a paged working set over a larger persistent store (page segments in/out by recency or relevance, à la virtual memory).
designSpace.tension: Payoff scales with how much of the context is literally repeated across turns/tasks — currency is input-only. On a genuinely novel hard task the informative delta (the part actually driving the hard reasoning) is by definition NOT a repeat of anything cached, so this saves prefill on the boilerplate around the problem and yields ~0% on the problem itself. Any eviction/paging policy also risks silently paging out the one segment (a safety constraint) that must never be evicted — the same failure mode as compaction, unless that segment is architecturally pinned.

designSpace.idea: Don't load into the primary context what isn't needed right now: fetch only relevant documents on demand (retrieval), or hand bulky exploration (grep a repo, read a manual, browse a page) to a cheap helper that returns a short summary instead of the raw material.
designSpace.tension: Input-currency, and its benefit is gated by an index or a summarizer already existing and being trustworthy. A rare-hard task is exactly the case where nothing relevant has been indexed yet (retrieval has nothing to return) and where a summary is most likely to silently drop the one caveat that mattered — the delegate's compression is a second, un-audited compaction step with the same landmine as history-summarization, just earlier in the pipeline.

designSpace.idea: Cache a previously-derived multi-step plan or induce a reusable parameterized 'skill' from an agent's own past traces, then replay/adapt it instead of re-deriving the approach from scratch each time.
designSpace.tension: Output-currency (fewer turns/tokens spent re-planning), but the saving is amortized: it requires the SAME task shape to recur, and injecting the growing catalog of skill descriptions into the prompt to make them findable raises input tokens on every call, including calls where none of them apply — net cost can rise on a workload dominated by one-off tasks, which is exactly the case this problem asks about. Zero benefit on the first-ever occurrence of a hard task.

designSpace.idea: Send each step to the cheapest model plausibly capable of it, escalating to a stronger model only on a failure signal, so easy work never pays frontier-model rates.
designSpace.tension: $-per-token currency, and it pays off across a MIX of easy and hard tasks in a workload, not on one hard task in isolation — a genuinely hard step fails on the cheap model, escalates, and the net cost on that instance is the frontier-model cost PLUS the wasted cheap attempt. Frequency here means difficulty-mix, not task repetition, and a rare-hard-task workload is the mix this family monetizes worst.

designSpace.idea: Instead of caching the PROCEDURE, cache the BOUNDARY: learn or author invariants ('never write outside the workspace', 'dry-run before any destructive command', 'no outbound network from a read-only tool') once, and apply them to every future action — including on a task type never seen before, because invariants generalize across dissimilar tasks in a way step-by-step plans don't.
designSpace.tension: Safety currency directly, cost currency indirectly (prevents expensive failed attempts and redo). If the invariants are induced from the agent's own small set of past failures they overfit and start blocking legitimate novel actions (false-positive rate rises as the task distribution shifts); and if they're self-induced by the same model they're meant to constrain, this family silently violates the authority-independence requirement unless a separate process authors or audits the induced set.

designSpace.family: Formal / runtime verification against a machine-checkable spec
designSpace.idea: Translate the safety or correctness policy into something a solver, theorem prover, or policy engine can check mechanically, then verify each PROPOSED action against that spec before it executes — a check whose cost is a function of the action's and spec's complexity, not of how many times the task type has recurred.
designSpace.tension: Frequency-independent safety currency — the strongest answer in this map to the rare-task crux — but it only proves the action stays inside a specified envelope, not that the task is being solved correctly; there is a soundness/completeness gap between 'safe' and 'right'. It also inherits an authoring burden: someone (or something) has to write the spec, and if the acting model writes its own envelope, the check reduces to self-certification.

designSpace.idea: Constrain the model's output distribution at the token level to a valid-action grammar, so malformed tool calls, syntax errors, and the retries they cause simply cannot be generated.
designSpace.tension: Output currency, frequency-independent — it works identically on the very first call. But it requires the valid-action schema to be authored up front (same authoring cost as the formal-verification family), and over-constraining the grammar can suppress the exploratory or unusual action a genuinely novel problem needs — safety-through-restriction traded against the latitude that hard, unprecedented tasks often require.

designSpace.idea: When a single task instance is internally repetitive (transform 200 files, rename a pattern across a tree), synthesize one small program that performs the whole operation instead of driving hundreds of individual agent turns — collapsing O(turns) output tokens into one synthesis call plus free deterministic execution.
designSpace.tension: The payoff is realized WITHIN one occurrence, so it is genuinely frequency-independent even for a task done once — but a single wrong synthesized script executes all 200 wrong operations at machine speed: the mechanism doesn't lower error probability, it multiplies the blast radius of any error it does contain, demanding the strongest pre-execution check of any family here. It also degrades on tasks whose next step depends on OBSERVING the previous step's result (interactive debugging, browsing) where a pre-written script can't react.

designSpace.idea: Use a cheap model or a deterministic tool to CHECK an expensive model's output or proposed action rather than regenerate it; escalate to costly re-derivation only when the check fails.
designSpace.tension: Output/$ currency, frequency-independent — checking cost is a function of the artifact's complexity, not task-repeat count, and it differs from cascades by checking AFTER production rather than routing BEFORE it. But the guarantee is only as strong as the verifier's soundness: a cheap verifier with false negatives lets errors through silently while presenting as a safety layer, which is worse than no verifier at all if it induces false confidence in the operator.

designSpace.idea: Make actions reversible by default — filesystem snapshot, DB transaction, copy-on-write, commit-before-mutate — so a wrong or failed action costs a rollback-and-retry instead of the agent re-deriving its entire plan in fresh tokens.
designSpace.tension: Output currency, frequency-independent — on a rare hard task, tokens are typically burned in RETRY LOOPS after a bad step, and this attacks that cost directly regardless of how many times the task type has recurred. But coverage is bounded by which action types are snapshot-able: a sent email, an external API side effect, or a real purchase cannot be rolled back, and building checkpoint infrastructure for the long tail of tool types is itself a standing engineering cost.

designSpace.idea: Gate actions by their SHAPE rather than the task's semantics — is this shell syntax destructive, does this write leave the workspace, is this HTTP verb mutating — over a small closed vocabulary of action primitives that stays the same no matter how novel the task is.
designSpace.tension: Safety currency, frequency-independent by construction, and naturally compaction-resistant if the triage rules live outside the transcript rather than in it. But it verifies the action isn't DANGEROUS, not that it's RIGHT for the task — a syntactically safe action can still be the wrong one (correctly deleting the wrong file) — so alone it cannot satisfy a no-correctness-regression requirement and must pair with a task-level check.

designSpace.idea: Spend compute proportional to per-step risk and uncertainty rather than uniformly across a task: a fast cheap path when confident, deliberate verification or a stronger model only when not.
designSpace.tension: Cuts both currencies unevenly and is frequency-independent in principle since it operates per-step rather than per-task-repetition. But if the confidence signal is the acting model's own self-report, it is both poorly calibrated and itself a form of self-certification — it only satisfies authority-independence if the trigger comes from an external/structural signal (e.g. the risk-triage family) rather than the model's introspection about its own output.

designSpace.idea: Defer high-risk, low-confidence, or structurally novel actions to a cheap asynchronous human check instead of spending more model inference trying to become more certain on its own.
designSpace.tension: Avoids further LLM cost on the escalated step entirely and is frequency-independent, safety-currency-dominant — but human attention is a real, scarce, and non-zero cost, and a poorly calibrated escalation threshold either floods a human with routine approvals (defeating the point of automating the agent) or under-escalates the cases that actually needed a person; the threshold itself has to be justified by an external signal, not by the agent's own say-so.

frame.hardestRequirement: Deliver both a cost saving AND a safety guarantee on a task instance the system has seen zero to two times before, where neither half is allowed to come from task-repetition history. Concretely: the check's authority must derive from something other than the acting model's own generation (no self-certification — rules out constraint-sets an agent induces from its own traces, specs it writes for itself, and its own confidence self-reports as sole gates), and the cost saving must be shown on that single instance against a mechanism-off counterfactual on the same instance, not amortized over a benchmark distribution. Together these two clauses eliminate every purely frequency-amortized family (skill/plan caching, cascades tuned to a workload's difficulty mix, corpus-mined invariants) as a *complete* answer, and force the surviving core mechanism to have a cost/safety payoff that is a function of the ACTION's structure or the TASK's own internal repetitiveness — not of how many times that task type has recurred before.

designs.name: Countinghouse — a metered tool-proxy runtime built on one thesis: amortize INSIDE the task instance, not across task repetitions; keep the law OUTSIDE the context window, not inside it.
designs.coreMechanism: Every side-effecting action (shell, file edit, HTTP, browser) passes through a teller's window: a deterministic tool proxy that sits between the agent and the world. The proxy runs four coupled components. (1) The Envelope: a machine-checkable contract (workspace bounds, host allowlist, irreversibility classes, resource ceilings) written in a small restricted predicate language, authored out-of-band before the task by a standing org policy plus a separate authoring model instance — ratified by a human for irreversible classes — compiled to deterministic checks plus SMT queries (e.g. prove a glob or pipeline's write set stays inside the workspace), enforced pre-execution, fail-closed on unclassifiable action shapes. Shape-based triage keys the solver only for mutating/irreversible actions; reads pass a microsecond allowlist, bounding overhead. (2) The Deed Ledger: every executed action emits a compact structured receipt (targets, diff, digest of observation) into an external store, with raw observations kept addressable; the transcript is then compacted aggressively and safely, because neither ground-truth state nor policy lives in it. (3) The Within-Instance Compiler: an anti-unification loop detector watches the ledger for structurally isomorphic action sequences WITHIN this one task; at k=3 repeats it pauses the agent, makes a single synthesis call producing one parameterized program for the remaining items, statically verifies the program's whole write-set against the Envelope, dry-run diff-tests it on the next item, then executes it deterministically — collapsing O(n) turns into O(1) calls. (4) Checkpointed execution: all mutations run copy-on-write (overlayfs/git-worktree; a staged outbox holds emails/POSTs until the irreversibility check or a human ack), so a bad step costs a rollback plus a short retry, not a transcript-poisoned re-derivation; an external stop-loss (same action failing k times) forces escalation instead of thrash — a structural trigger, never the model's self-report.
designs.savesMagnitude: Input: ledger-backed compaction replaces the growing transcript with receipts plus on-demand paging — 40-70% prefill reduction on long tasks (late turns are transcript-dominated), now safe because policy is out-of-band; the envelope-hash-stable system prefix is prompt-cache-friendly, stacking with the 41-80% prefill discount. Zero standing input tax from skill catalogs: synthesized programs are per-instance and archived out-of-band, never injected into prompts (avoids the measured +9.7% input / +5.5% net-cost trap). Output: within-instance compilation collapses an n-item repetitive segment from n per-item turns to ~1 synthesis + verification — e.g. 50 items at ~800 output tokens each becomes ~97% savings on that segment, ~30-60% at task level when internal repetition exists, exact no-op (0 cost) when it does not; checkpoint-retry makes a failure cost ~10-20% of a full re-derivation, worth another 15-30% output on hard tasks with 2-3 failures; the stop-loss caps worst-case thrash. Every saving is computable per instance against a counterfactual: (remaining items × observed per-item cost of the first k items) vs the synthesis call; observed pre-rollback re-derivation length vs retry length; per-turn prefill with vs without ledger compaction on the same instance.
designs.correctnessMechanism: Authority is never the acting model. The Envelope is authored by a separate process (standing policy + a differently-instructed authoring instance + human ratification for irreversible classes), compiled to deterministic code and SMT queries, and enforced by the proxy BEFORE execution — fail-closed: an action shape the triage cannot classify is refused or escalated, never silently run. Safety (in-envelope) is deliberately separated from rightness: synthesized programs must additionally pass a dry-run diff against what the agent's own per-item action produces on the next item before batch execution, irreversible actions are never batch-compiled, and all mutations are transactional so post-hoc audit sampling plus rollback bounds the blast radius of any error that slips through. Correctness is not regressed relative to baseline: the gate only blocks, the compiler only replaces actions it has diff-validated, and rollback converts failures the baseline agent would pay for in full re-derivation into cheap local retries — which raises reliability (errors caught pre-execution or reverted) while cutting cost.
designs.survivesCompaction: Fully, by construction: the Envelope, the Deed Ledger, the checkpoints, and the stop-loss all live outside the context window in the proxy's own store. The agent can lose every old turn — including any memory of its constraints — and the gate still enforces the identical contract on the next tool call, because enforcement happens at the tool boundary, not in the prompt. This directly closes the measured landmine (0% → 30-59% violation rates when the policy fell out of a summary): here the policy was never in the summary's custody to begin with. Compaction is inverted from a risk into a savings lever: the ledger makes aggressive transcript compaction safe, and lets a compacted agent cheaply re-hydrate exactly the state slice it needs by querying receipts instead of re-reading history.
designs.rareHardTaskMechanism: Three mechanisms whose payoff is a function of the instance's own structure, never of recurrence count. (1) The Within-Instance Compiler: loop detection runs over THIS task's deed ledger, so a task seen exactly once still amortizes — the first 3 of 50 file-transforms are done by hand, the remaining 47 by one verified program; the counterfactual (47 × observed per-item cost) is computed from this same instance, satisfying per-instance measurability with no corpus. On a genuinely non-repetitive task the detector never fires: a true no-op, never negative ROI. (2) Checkpoint-retry: on rare hard tasks output tokens die in retry loops after bad steps; rollback makes the marginal failure cost a snapshot-revert plus a short focused retry instead of a full re-plan over a poisoned transcript — frequency-independent, measurable on the instance. (3) The Envelope's check cost is O(action complexity), not O(times seen): the SMT proof that `rm -rf $DIR/**` stays inside the workspace costs the same milliseconds on the first-ever occurrence as the thousandth, and fail-closed refusal covers exactly the case where no held-out failure history exists to have caught the bad action. Ledger-backed compaction additionally keeps a long ONE-OFF task's prefill from growing quadratically. Nothing here mines prior traces, injects a catalog, or needs a difficulty-mix to monetize.
failureModes: Compiler false generalization: anti-unification matches superficially similar but semantically distinct items and the dry-run diff on item k+1 misses a divergence that first appears at item 37 — mitigated by transactional execution, audit sampling, and never batch-compiling irreversible actions, but a rollback plus partial redo still costs real tokens.

Envelope mis-calibration: too tight and it refuses the legitimate exploratory action a novel task genuinely needs (false-positive stalls, escalation latency); too loose and it is safety theater — the amendment path (human-ratified envelope edit) works but reintroduces human turnaround into an automated flow.

Fail-closed friction on novel tool shapes: the first use of an unclassifiable action type always escalates; a workload dominated by genuinely new tools turns the human ratifier into the bottleneck the agent was meant to remove.

Safe is not right: an action can be provably in-envelope and still wrong for the task (correctly-scoped deletion of the wrong file); task-level correctness still rests on the acting model plus dry-run diffs, and the operator must not read the gate's approval as a correctness certificate — false confidence is the worst outcome of a sound-looking verifier.

Ledger receipts are themselves compression: a deed summary can drop the caveat that mattered, the same landmine moved earlier in the pipeline — mitigated by keeping raw observations addressable for re-paging rather than deleting them, but a bad relevance judgment still costs a re-fetch or an error.

Overhead inversion on small tasks: envelope negotiation plus proxy machinery can exceed what a 5-turn task ever spends — the self-gating threshold (skip heavy machinery below a task-size/risk floor) must exist and can itself misjudge.

Staged-outbox coverage gap: interactive external flows that require synchronous side effects (a login handshake, a paginated purchase flow) cannot be held in an outbox; those actions fall back to per-action gating with human ack, capping savings on browser-heavy work.
roadmap: M1 — Teller's window: build the tool proxy intercepting shell/file/HTTP calls with deterministic shape-triage, workspace-bound and host-allowlist checks, and fail-closed refusal; measure per-action latency overhead and false-positive refusal rate on a standard agent benchmark; wire the SMT backend for path/write-set proofs on mutating shapes only.

M2 — Deed Ledger and safe compaction: emit structured receipts for every executed action, implement transcript compaction with ledger-pointer re-hydration, and run the landmine test — verify policy-violation rate stays at 0% under aggressive compaction while measuring same-instance prefill reduction (target 40%+ on long tasks).

M3 — Checkpointed execution: overlayfs/git-worktree snapshots plus the staged outbox for network effects; implement rollback-retry and the structural stop-loss; measure retry token cost vs observed full re-derivation cost on injected-failure tasks.

M4 — Within-Instance Compiler: anti-unification loop detector over the ledger, single-call program synthesis, static envelope verification of the program's write-set, dry-run diff gate, deterministic execution; validate per-instance counterfactual accounting on internally repetitive one-off tasks (bulk edits, tree-wide renames, scrape-and-transform).

M5 — Composition and self-gating: pin the envelope-hash-stable prefix for prompt caching, route synthesis and envelope-authoring calls to appropriately-sized models, add the task-size floor that skips heavy machinery on trivially cheap work, and publish end-to-end dual-currency (input vs output) mechanism-on/off results per instance on a rare-hard-task suite.

designs.name: PORTCULLIS — Warranted Execution on a Transactional Substrate (a gate that, like its namesake, falls shut when anything fails)
designs.coreMechanism: Every side-effecting action the agent proposes must transit an out-of-process gate daemon sitting on the tool-execution path (a proxy the model physically cannot bypass — never a prompt). To pass, the action carries a "warrant": a machine-readable claim of its effects in a small closed effect-vocabulary (paths written, verbs, egress class, reversibility). The gate checks the warrant against a two-layer policy: (1) a human-authored Constitution of ~20 generic invariants (workspace containment, no-egress classes, dry-run-before-destructive, irreversible-implies-human) forming a permission CEILING, and (2) an optional task-specific envelope the acting LLM may propose but which is admitted only if an SMT solver proves it a strict REFINEMENT of the Constitution — monotone narrowing: the model can shrink its own permissions, never grant them, so verification authority never derives from the generative process. The gate runs atop a copy-on-write transactional workspace: every gated action is snapshot-first, so an in-workspace mistake costs a rollback, not a token-burning recovery arc. And when one task instance is internally repetitive, the agent may submit a single contract-carrying program (code + declared effect footprint + postcondition); the gate verifies it by static effect analysis plus a k-sample dry-run in a CoW fork, then executes all N operations under a runtime monitor that kills on first envelope exit. Tiered triage self-gates the machinery: pure in-workspace reads pass in microseconds; the solver and dry-runs engage only on structurally risky or batch actions; irreversible external actions (send, purchase, API mutation) are constitutionally non-delegable and always escalate to a human.
designs.savesMagnitude: INPUT: the standing safety-policy prose (typically 1–3k tokens) is deleted from every turn and replaced by a ~50-token pointer, because enforcement is structural, not textual; the violated clause is injected only on rejection ("policy paging by violation"). Roughly 10–30% of per-turn prefill on policy-heavy agents, and it COMPOUNDS with prompt caching because the prefix becomes more stable, not less. OUTPUT/CALLS: contract-carrying batch programs collapse O(N)-turn mechanical phases into 1 synthesis call + k sample checks — 10–100x on those phases, ~25–35% of total output tokens on mixed real instances; separately, each pre-execution catch converts a typical 5–20-turn post-hoc recovery arc into one reject+repair turn. $-PER-TOKEN (indirect): because the gate bounds any model's blast radius, cheap-model routing can be used far more aggressively — verification underwrites the router. OVERHEAD is self-gated: a benign novel task with no risky actions and no internal repetition pays approximately zero (Tier-0/1 static checks only), satisfying the never-negative-ROI floor.
designs.correctnessMechanism: Authority-independent by construction, layered by risk tier. (1) The Constitution is human-authored, compiled to solver-checkable predicates, and stored in a policy service the model has no write path to. (2) Any LLM-proposed task envelope is admitted only via a solver-proved refinement proof — monotone narrowing means no self-certification path exists anywhere in the design; the generative process can only ever reduce its own permissions. (3) Per-action warrants are checked deterministically (static shape analysis over the closed vocabulary); Tier-2 actions are discharged by the SMT solver; timeout or unclassifiable shape fails CLOSED to rejection or human escalation, never silent execution. (4) Batch programs additionally require a postcondition verified on k dry-run samples in a CoW fork before the monitored full run. (5) Irreversible actions always require a human — no history of prior successes can earn them autonomy. (6) The gate's only outputs are pass, reject-with-clause, or escalate — it never mutates anything itself, so its worst failure is a stall, never silent corruption; and because rejections return the exact violated clause, the agent retries better-informed rather than blind, which is why the mechanism raises rather than lowers task success. The transactional substrate makes even wrong-but-in-envelope actions cheaply revertible, and counterfactual forks (sealed-sandbox replay of the blocked or mechanism-off branch from the pre-action snapshot) give a same-instance on/off audit of every intervention.
designs.survivesCompaction: Yes, by construction rather than by mitigation. The Constitution, the admitted envelope (content-addressed by hash), and the warrant checker live in the out-of-process gate daemon on the tool path — every action physically transits it regardless of what the transcript remembers. Compact the context window to nothing and enforcement is unchanged: the agent may lose AWARENESS of the policy, but its first violating attempt returns the exact violated clause as a rejection message, so the policy re-enters context precisely when needed at clause-size input cost instead of living as evictable prose. The measured 0%-to-30–59% compaction-violation failure class is structurally impossible here because no constraint's authority ever resided in the window in the first place.
designs.rareHardTaskMechanism: Three payoffs that are functions of the INSTANCE itself, none of recurrence history. (a) First-occurrence safety: shape triage and Constitution checks are functions of the ACTION's structure over a closed primitive vocabulary — "rm -rf outside workspace" is classified identically on occurrence #1 of a never-before-seen task, with no corpus, no mining, no calibration. (b) First-occurrence cost, two concrete channels: hard tasks burn most tokens in post-error recovery arcs and in mechanically repetitive phases WITHIN the single instance. The gate converts the former — the wrong action is rejected BEFORE the side effect that would have spawned a 5–20-turn debugging arc, costing one reject+repair turn instead. Contract-carrying batch compilation converts the latter — "migrate these 214 config files," done ONCE, becomes one synthesized program + 5-sample dry-run + monitored deterministic run instead of 214 agent turns; the payoff is realized inside that single occurrence. Per-instance measurability is built in: the CoW snapshot taken before each gated action lets the system replay the mechanism-off branch in a sealed sandbox, yielding a same-instance on/off comparison — no benchmark distribution needed. (c) Occurrences #2–3 get a bonus, never a dependency: admitted envelopes and verified programs are content-addressed and re-offered by deterministic structural match AT THE GATE — surfaced as one line, not a prompt-injected catalog — and must re-verify against current state before replay. So reuse adds zero input-token bloat and zero unearned authority, and a genuinely novel task where nothing matches is a measured no-op.
failureModes: Safe-but-wrong gap: the gate proves containment, not task-rightness — a correctly-formed deletion of the WRONG in-workspace file passes; rollback and postconditions soften it, but semantic wrongness inside the envelope is honestly out of scope and needs the agent's own judgment plus the transactional net.

Vocabulary lag: an action shape outside the closed effect vocabulary (opaque binary, novel tool) fail-closes to escalation; if the toolset outgrows the vocabulary, humans get flooded with approvals and the latitude genuinely exploratory tasks need gets suppressed.

Constitution bugs are a single point of failure: one mis-authored invariant either stalls legitimate work everywhere (false positives) or silently permits a harm class (false negatives) — the ceiling is only as sound as its human authors and needs its own review discipline.

Sample-verification escape on batches: the k-sample dry-run misses the pathological item N-3; the runtime monitor catches envelope EXITS, but an in-envelope wrong transform hits all N at machine speed before rollback — the transaction bounds the blast radius, it does not eliminate it.

Unmediated channels break everything: any tool not proxied through the gate (agent writes a cron job, spawns a detached process, finds an unproxied network path) is a total bypass; the executor boundary must be exhaustively enumerated or the guarantee is theatre.

Solver pathology: predicate blowup forces a timeout, which fail-closes to escalation — correct but costly; a complex-but-benign action can degenerate the system into human-in-the-loop and erode the cost story on exactly the hard tasks it targets.

Counterfactual mispricing: the sealed-sandbox replay prices the mechanism-off branch approximately (a real recovery arc might have unfolded differently); the per-instance savings ledger is evidence, not proof, and must be labeled as such to avoid false confidence.
roadmap: M1 — Total mediation + transactional substrate: proxy every tool call through the gate daemon; CoW snapshots (overlayfs/btrfs or a git-object store) before every gated action; deterministic shape triage over the closed primitive vocabulary, fail-closed on unclassifiable. Exit: zero unmediated side effects on a red-team bypass suite; <1% latency overhead; zero task-success regression vs the bare agent.

M2 — Constitution + refinement solver: author the ~20-invariant Constitution, compile to SMT; implement monotone-narrowing envelope admission and reject-with-clause feedback; delete standing policy prose from prompts. Exit: 0% violation rate under forced transcript compaction (vs the 30–59% failure class), with the measured per-turn input-token drop documented.

M3 — Contract-carrying batch programs: warrant DSL for program effect footprints; static effect analysis; k-sample dry-run in CoW forks; monitored execution with kill-on-first-envelope-exit; postcondition checks. Exit: same-instance on/off comparison shows >=5x output-token cut on internally-repetitive instances at equal-or-better success.

M4 — Counterfactual fork ledger: automatic sealed-sandbox replay of blocked and mechanism-off branches from pre-action snapshots; per-instance dual-currency accounting (tokens saved vs overhead spent, catches vs false positives). Exit: every gate intervention priced on its own instance, no benchmark averaging required.

M5 — Composition layer: gate-underwritten aggressive model routing (cheap models earn wider use because their blast radius is bounded); content-addressed envelope/program re-offer with mandatory re-verification for occurrences #2–3, surfaced at the gate rather than prompt-injected. Exit: net dollar reduction on a mixed workload with no correctness regression and zero growth in per-call prompt overhead from the artifact library.

designs.name: PACT — Proof-Carrying Acts under Chartered Transactions
designs.coreMechanism: Move safety out of the transcript and cost out of the loop. Three durable planes live OUTSIDE the context window: (1) a CHARTER — the task's permission envelope expressed in a small decidable predicate algebra (path prefixes, finite tool/verb vocabularies, string patterns, linear resource bounds) that compiles to SMT; it is seeded by a human-owned standing workspace charter and specialized per-task by a separate 'surveyor' model instance that sees only the task statement plus observed workspace facts, under a MONOTONE NARROWING law: LLM authorship may only shrink the allowed set, never widen it, so self-authorship can never grant powers — widening always requires the human. (2) a deterministic GATE in the harness's tool-execution path that verifies every side-effecting action pre-execution against the charter, fail-closed, with tiered effort (Tier 0: microsecond AST/shape triage for read-only acts; Tier 1: predicate evaluation; Tier 2: SMT for novel shapes and batch programs; Tier 3: refuse-or-escalate presenting the single undischarged predicate as a one-tap human question), executing each approved act inside a copy-on-write transaction so wrong-but-allowed acts cost a rollback, not a re-derivation. (3) an append-only LEDGER of verified acts + post-state digests that becomes the agent's ground-truth memory, letting the harness compact the transcript aggressively — the gate LICENSES compaction because the constraint's authority never lived in the window. Cost is then attacked inside the single instance: a loop detector watches the ledger for ≥2-3 structurally similar acts on THIS task, compiles the remaining N−k into one parameterized program whose entire parameter space is checked symbolically at the gate and whose postcondition is sample-validated inside the transaction before machine-speed apply — collapsing O(N) agent turns into O(1) synthesis, with per-element fallback to ordinary agentic handling for any element that fails its postcondition.
designs.savesMagnitude: INPUT: 30-70% prefill on long instances — the gate makes aggressive transcript compaction safe (harvesting the compaction-class savings the field measures at 41-80% but currently can't take safely), plus ledger paging replaces resident history with a small state capsule; and ~0 per-call input inflation because the charter is ENFORCED, not injected (vs +9.7% input growth for injected skill specs; only a pinned ~100-token digest rides in context, as UX not authority). OUTPUT: on instances with internal repetition, the batched fraction collapses (N−k)/N of its turns — e.g. a 200-file transform goes from ~200 per-item turns to 1 synthesis + 1 symbolic check, >90% of that fraction's output tokens; retry-spiral aversion (bad acts blocked before they corrupt state; wrong-but-allowed acts roll back instead of being re-derived) is worth an estimated 15-40% of output on hard tasks where recovery dominates. FLOOR: on a genuinely novel, non-repetitive, read-only task the system self-gates to Tier-0 only — ≈0% saved, ≈0% overhead, never negative ROI.
designs.correctnessMechanism: Authority independence by construction: the verifier is deterministic code plus an off-the-shelf SMT solver; permissive authority flows only from the human-owned standing charter; the acting model and the surveyor can author predicates only in the narrowing direction, so the check never reduces to self-certification. Gating is pre-execution and fail-closed: an action whose predicates cannot be discharged with confidence is refused or escalated with the exact failing predicate — a novel shape needs no failure history to be caught. The gate honestly proves ALLOWED, not RIGHT, so correctness is carried by two further layers: every compiled batch program must ship an acceptance postcondition that is validated on 2-3 sample elements inside the CoW transaction before generalizing to all N (sample-validate-then-generalize), with automatic per-element rollback and fallback to per-item agentic handling on any postcondition failure; and every side-effecting act runs in a snapshot transaction, so allowed-but-wrong acts are cheap resets. No-regression argument: every mechanism degrades to the unassisted-baseline behavior on failure (compilation falls back to agent turns; a gate denial costs one revision turn but averts a corrupted-state spiral; ledger paging rehydrates verbatim detail on demand), so task success is bounded below by the baseline while blocked pre-execution errors push reliability above it. Per-instance measurability is built in: the loop detector triggers only after k acts whose cost was measured ON THIS INSTANCE, so the counterfactual (measured per-act cost × N−k vs actual synthesis+verify cost) is provable on a single occurrence with no benchmark distribution.
designs.survivesCompaction: Yes — by architecture, not by effort. The charter, gate, and ledger live in the harness and on disk (hash-pinned, versioned); enforcement never reads the transcript, so there is nothing compaction can drop that weakens the check. The measured 0%→30-59% violation cliff cannot occur because the policy was never resident in the window in the first place. The harness re-injects the ~100-token charter digest after every compaction event purely so the agent doesn't propose doomed actions; even if that digest were lost, the worst case is denial-thrash — gate denials whose machine-generated explanations re-teach the constraint in one turn — never a violation. The inversion is the point: compaction stops being a safety hazard and becomes an actively harvested input saving, applied more aggressively BECAUSE the gate exists.
designs.rareHardTaskMechanism: Nothing in the payoff is a function of task-type recurrence; every lever keys on the action's structure or the instance's own internals. Concretely, four mechanisms: (1) INTRA-INSTANCE COMPILATION — repetition is harvested WITHIN the single occurrence: the loop detector fires on this task's own ledger after k≈2-3 structurally similar acts, compiles the remaining N−k into one gate-verified program, and the saving is computed against the measured cost of those same k acts — a same-instance counterfactual requiring zero prior corpus. A hard task done once that touches 40 files still pays out on 37 of them. (2) AVERTED RETRY SPIRALS — on rare hard tasks most output tokens burn in recovery after a bad step; the gate blocks the bad step pre-execution and the CoW transaction turns wrong-but-allowed steps into rollbacks, a payoff proportional to the action's blast radius, not to how often the task type recurred. (3) COMPACTION LICENSE — a first-ever long task can be compacted hard from turn one because the constraint's authority is extra-contextual, so the input saving starts on occurrence #1. (4) FREQUENCY-FLAT CHECKING — the gate's cost and coverage are functions of predicate complexity and the standing charter, identical on occurrence #1 and #1000; a truly novel action shape fails closed to a one-predicate human question rather than depending on held-out failure history. And the cold-start floor is explicit: a novel task with no side effects and no internal repetition triggers no surveyor call, no solver, no compiler — a true no-op.
failureModes: Over-narrow envelope: a cautious surveyor plus the monotone-narrowing law means the agent cannot widen its own permissions, so legitimate novel actions get blocked — denial-thrash burns output tokens and floods the human with escalations if the standing charter was authored badly; mitigation is the one-predicate escalation UX and shipped default charters per workspace archetype, but the failure is real.

Semantic gap: the predicate algebra expresses shape and scope ('writes stay under /workspace', 'no network from read-only tools'), not intent — 'emailed the WRONG Claire' is allowed-but-harmful and the gate will pass it; the acceptance-postcondition layer narrows this but cannot close it, and the system must publish an honest boundary statement rather than imply semantic safety.

Batch blast radius: a compiled program that is inside the envelope but wrong executes N wrong operations at machine speed; sample-validate-then-generalize and transactional apply contain filesystem cases, but irreversible tools (send, purchase, external POST) must be charter-marked non-batchable and never compiled — a misclassified tool here is the worst failure in the design.

Solver fragility: predicates drifting outside the decidable fragment cause Tier-2 timeouts, forcing Tier-3 fail-closed escalations that bottleneck on the human; the algebra must stay brutally small, which limits expressiveness.
TOCTOU: verifying against a snapshot the world mutates before execution — gate-and-execute must hold one snapshot lock, and external-world actions (web, other processes) can't be fully locked.

Counterfactual optimism: the first k acts used to price the counterfactual may be more expensive than later acts would have been (agent learning-curve within the instance), inflating claimed savings; report bands, not points.

Ledger paging is still compression: verbatim and rehydratable, but the agent must KNOW to rehydrate the one buried fact that matters — a retrieval-failure mode, softer than summarization's silent drop but nonzero.
roadmap: M1 — Charter kernel: implement the decidable predicate algebra (path prefixes, finite tool/verb sets, string patterns, linear resource bounds), its compiler to SMT-LIB2 and its fast deterministic evaluator; define the standing-charter file format plus default charters for common workspace archetypes; property-test that the surveyor pathway structurally CANNOT widen (monotone narrowing enforced by the type of the composition operator, not by review).

M2 — The Gate in one real harness: wrap the tool-execution hook path of an off-the-shelf agent harness with tiered triage (Tier-0 AST shape check through Tier-3 one-predicate human escalation), copy-on-write transactional workspace (overlayfs or git-worktree snapshots), and gate-and-execute under a single snapshot lock; hold overhead to <1% of instance tokens and <100ms p50 gate latency, with the self-gating tier ladder proven on read-only workloads (true no-op).

M3 — Ledger + compaction license: append-only verified-act ledger with post-state digests and a rehydration API; a harness compaction policy whose aggressiveness keys on gate presence; single-instance A/B under forced compaction measuring violation rate (target: 0% with the policy fully evicted from context) and prefill token delta.

M4 — Intra-instance compiler: structural act-similarity loop detector over the ledger, synthesis of a parameterized program, symbolic whole-parameter-space verification at the gate, the sample-validate-then-generalize postcondition protocol with per-element rollback and agentic fallback; ship the built-in same-instance counterfactual meter (measured k-act cost × (N−k) vs actual synthesis+verify+apply).

M5 — Rare-hard-task evaluation + red team: a suite of hard tasks each run EXACTLY ONCE, mechanism-on vs mechanism-off from identical workspace snapshots, reporting dual-currency token deltas, success rate, and violations; adversarial probing of the semantic gap (allowed-but-wrong actions) and of irreversible-tool classification, culminating in a published honest boundary statement of what the charter can and cannot express.

designs.name: Interlock — an effect-escrow sidecar for LLM agents (a service-mesh proxy for tool traffic: the Envoy of agent actions)
designs.coreMechanism: Interlock is a thin interposition shim at the one boundary every agent harness already shares — the tool-call interface. All side-effecting actions (shell, file edit, HTTP, browser) pass through a sidecar process that (1) checks each proposed action against a machine-checkable permission envelope that lives in the sidecar, never in the transcript; (2) executes risky or batched actions in ESCROW — a copy-on-write shadow (overlayfs / git worktree / DB transaction) — then verifies the resulting effect-trace (every path touched, every verb, every egress) against the envelope plus the task's own tests before atomically committing or rolling back; and (3) maintains a small machine-owned progress ledger (committed actions, checkpoint ids, ground-truth workspace state) outside the context window. Authority is two-tier and monotonic: a human-authored, task-independent FLOOR policy (workspace jail, egress allowlist, destructive-command lexicon) is active from action #1 and can never be loosened by any generated artifact; task-specific envelope DELTAS are drafted lazily by a separate model call but may only TIGHTEN the floor — any widening escalates to a human — so the operative authority is always deterministic code + the human floor, never the acting model grading itself. The sidecar is deliberately not a harness: it supercharges the existing levers rather than replacing them — it makes aggressive compaction SAFE (policy no longer depends on the transcript), makes cheap-model routing SAFE on novel tasks (the gate catches the cheap model's dangerous mistakes pre-commit, and rejection/test-failure is the external escalation signal instead of self-reported confidence), gives each sub-agent an attenuated sub-envelope so delegation can't launder authority, and pins a ~100-token advisory contract stub at a cache-stable prefix position so prompt caching keeps paying.
designs.savesMagnitude: Three per-instance meters, each with a logged counterfactual. (a) Turn collapse via checked macro-execution: when a task is internally repetitive (transform 240 files), one synthesized script escrow-verified and committed replaces ~240 agent turns; since every avoided turn saves BOTH a full generation (output) and a full prefill of the then-current context (input), this is 60-90% of both currencies on such tasks — the meter records N_avoided × (context_size_at_that_point + typical_generation). (b) Safe aggressive compaction: because enforcement never depends on the transcript, compaction can be turned up hard and the agent rehydrated from the ~1-2KB ground-truth ledger instead of the transcript — 20-40% input savings on long non-repetitive tasks. (c) Cheap failure: rollback-and-retry from a checkpoint replaces the agent reasoning its way back from a bad state — 10-30% output savings on hard tasks (which fail often), plus 2-5× $-per-token where gate-protected routing lets a small model drive envelope-covered steps. Worst case on a short novel task that stays inside the floor: ~zero — the floor check is microseconds of deterministic code, the delta envelope is never drafted (lazy), no extra model calls occur.
designs.correctnessMechanism: Layered, with honest scope for each layer. SAFETY (allowed-ness) is mechanical and fail-closed: every action is checked pre-execution against floor + delta by deterministic code, with an SMT solver for path/glob/quota/ordering constraints; unrecognized action shapes or solver timeouts default to refuse-or-escalate, never silent execution. Authority independence holds because the floor is human-authored, deltas can only tighten it, and the checker is code — no self-certification anywhere in the loop; the acting model's confidence is never a gate input (external signals — gate rejection, shadow test failure — drive escalation instead). CORRECTNESS (right-ness) is not claimed by the solver; it comes from escrow: risky and batched actions run in the shadow first, the effect-trace and workspace diff are inspected, the repo's own test suite (or a task-supplied check) runs against the shadow, and only then does the commit land — so a compliant-but-wrong action fails observably and rolls back for the cost of a snapshot restore, not a token-burning undo derivation. Net effect on success rate is non-negative by construction: the layer only ever blocks/rolls back actions, plus structured rejections cite the violated clause so the model course-corrects in one turn instead of thrashing.
designs.survivesCompaction: Yes, by architecture rather than by discipline: the envelope, the floor policy, and the progress ledger live in the sidecar process keyed to the session, and are evaluated on every tool call regardless of what the transcript contains — the transcript can be compacted to a single sentence and the gate still blocks. This inverts the 0%→30% compaction landmine: instead of hoping the summary retains the policy, Interlock makes the policy unconditionally enforced and then EXPLOITS that to compact more aggressively for input savings. The advisory contract stub re-injected at the cached prefix helps the model PROPOSE compliant actions (reducing rejected-attempt churn), but enforcement never depends on the model remembering anything.
designs.rareHardTaskMechanism: Every payoff is a function of the INSTANCE's structure, not of task-type recurrence — four concrete frequency-independent mechanisms. (1) Checked macro-execution monetizes the task's INTERNAL repetitiveness on its very first occurrence: 'migrate 240 config files, never touch release/* or CI secrets' becomes one synthesized script, statically analyzed, run in an overlayfs shadow, its effect-trace diffed against the envelope (catching the release-branch rule mechanically at diff time, long after compaction would have eaten it from context), test-gated, then committed atomically — ~10 turns instead of ~250, metered on that single instance against the mechanism-off counterfactual. (2) Cheap rollback monetizes the task's ERROR RATE, which is highest exactly on hard novel tasks: retry loops restart from a snapshot plus a ledger-rehydrated compact state instead of the agent spending turns reasoning about how to undo. (3) Ledger-backed compaction monetizes the task's LENGTH: hard one-off tasks are long, and safe-to-compact transcripts cut prefill on every remaining turn. (4) Gate-enabled routing monetizes PER-STEP difficulty spread within one task: a cheap model may attempt steps because its dangerous errors are blocked pre-commit and its wrong-but-safe errors fail visibly in escrow and roll back — no workload mix or repetition history required. Cold start is genuinely covered: the floor ships with the layer and needs zero prior traces; the delta is one lazy model call made only when the agent first pushes past the floor; on a task that never does, the whole apparatus is a no-op costing microseconds per action.
failureModes: Over-tight envelopes (false positives): a wrong-but-conservative delta blocks legitimate novel actions; the agent burns tokens proposing rejected variants. Mitigation — rejections cite the exact violated clause, widenings get a one-touch human escalation path — bounds but does not eliminate the churn.

The semantic gap: the solver proves ALLOWED, not RIGHT — deleting the wrong file inside the workspace passes the gate. Escrow + tests catch only what tests cover; on tasks with weak checks, compliant-wrong actions commit. Interlock must never be sold as a correctness prover.

Irreversible-effect coverage gap: a sent email, a real purchase, an external API POST cannot be escrowed or rolled back; the floor forces these through human escalation, which reintroduces latency and scarce human attention — an under-tuned threshold either floods the human or stalls unattended runs.

Shadow/commit divergence (TOCTOU): the world changes between dry-run and commit (another process writes the repo, a remote resource moves); requires workspace leases and cheap commit-time re-validation, and residual divergence can still slip through on shared systems.

Effect-trace incompleteness: sandbox tracing can miss side channels (time-dependent behavior, effects mediated by an allowed network call), so the verified trace understates the real footprint precisely where sandboxing is weakest.

Advisory-stub blindness: enforcement survives compaction but the model's MEMORY of the rules does not — a model that keeps forgetting proposes non-compliant actions repeatedly; nothing unsafe runs, but rejection churn eats part of the savings on very long tasks.

Solver/complexity stalls: a pathological delta (huge glob sets, deep quota interactions) hits SMT timeouts; fail-closed then means escalation stalls in unattended operation — timeouts must degrade to a coarser syntactic check plus escalation, not to a hang.
roadmap: M1 — The shim and the floor (weeks): an MCP-proxy/harness-hook sidecar intercepting all tool calls; human-authored floor policy (path jail, egress allowlist, destructive-command lexicon, mutating-verb triage); fail-closed with structured rejections; per-action decision log plus the counterfactual meter that every later milestone reports through.

M2 — Escrow and rollback: copy-on-write shadow execution (overlayfs / git worktree / DB transactions), effect-trace capture and diffing, atomic commit/rollback, checkpoint-wired retry loops; measure output-token savings on induced failures, same instance on vs off.

M3 — Checked macro-execution: the script-synthesis path — static analysis of the synthesized program, shadow run, envelope diff-check on the full effect trace, test gate, atomic commit; per-instance turn-collapse metering against the projected turn-by-turn counterfactual.

M4 — Lazy task-delta envelopes: a separate drafting model call triggered only when the agent pushes past the floor; monotonic tightening enforced by construction, SMT-backed path/glob/quota checks, human escalation for widenings and irreversibles; cache-stable contract stub injection.

M5 — Composition kits and evaluation: ledger-driven safe compaction with ground-truth rehydration, gate-enabled cheap-model routing, attenuated sub-envelopes for sub-agents; an A/B harness that replays a single recorded task with the layer on vs off to publish per-instance dual-currency numbers on one-shot hard tasks.

designs.name: CONTINUO — the Score-and-Warrant runtime (the transcript is not the computer; the program is)
designs.coreMechanism: Invert the standard agent loop: stop treating the LLM as the interpreter and the context window as RAM. At task start the frontier model emits, once, two artifacts into a runtime store: (1) a "Score" — a typed PARTIAL PROGRAM over a small closed action vocabulary, in which everything the model is confident is deterministic gets fully compiled (a loop over 200 files is one loop, not 200 turns), and every point of genuine uncertainty is declared as a typed HOLE with an explicit dataflow contract ("inputs: these 3 file excerpts + this error; output type: patch confined to scope S; effect budget: none"); and (2) a proposed task Warrant that can only NARROW a standing, operator-authored environment Warrant — a monotone restriction whose subset relation is verified mechanically (lattice meet, solver-checked), so model-authored spec text can never widen authority. A deterministic runtime then interprets the Score: compiled stretches execute for zero model tokens after their loop bodies are symbolically certified against the Warrant ONCE (one abstract-interpretation proof covers all iterations; per-action concrete checking is the fallback); each hole triggers a minimal-context model call carrying only its declared inputs plus the relevant Warrant clauses — never the transcript. Every primitive effect, compiled or hole-produced, passes the fail-closed Warrant checker before it runs; reversible effect classes execute inside copy-on-write transactions; deterministic acceptance predicates (tests green, schema validates, diff confined to scope) sit at program joints and re-open a bounded hole with failure evidence when they fail, instead of resuming a drifted transcript. The LLM becomes a code generator plus an oracle for holes; the interpreter is deterministic code, and the conversation transcript becomes disposable scaffolding.
designs.savesMagnitude: INPUT: 60-90% on long multi-step tasks, and it stacks with (rather than depends on) prompt caching. A reactive agent re-pays a growing transcript every turn — cumulative prefill is roughly quadratic in turns, and caching only discounts the stable prefix while the suffix grows unboundedly. CONTINUO's per-hole calls carry ~0.3-3K tokens of declared inputs versus 30-200K of transcript, and the payload never grows with task length. OUTPUT/CALLS: 30-70% on tasks with internal deterministic structure — compiled stretches collapse O(n) act-observe turns into 1 synthesis call + free execution (200-file case: ~8 calls total vs 200+), and pre-execution gating converts each would-be failed attempt (execute, observe error, re-plan — 3 paid steps) into one free checker rejection. Overhead honestly stated: one triage call + one synthesis call that is longer than a single act call, plus solver time (milliseconds-to-seconds, no tokens). Self-gating: a cheap triage step routes tasks with no compilable structure (estimated <5 steps, or fully observation-driven) into plain reactive mode with Warrant gating only — the cost machinery is skipped, safety is not. Floor: on a genuinely unstructured task the Score degenerates to a chain of holes ≈ a normal agent, delta ≈ one wasted triage call, never materially negative ROI.
designs.correctnessMechanism: Authority independence via the monotone-narrowing lattice: the environment Warrant (filesystem/network scopes, irreversibility classes, budgets, escalation rules) is authored once per WORKSPACE by the operator — versioned deterministic policy code plus a human, never the acting model. The acting model may only propose restrictions of it; the checker proves the subset relation mechanically, so nothing model-authored ever grants what the standing policy withheld — no self-certification by construction. Pre-execution and fail-closed: every primitive action is checked against the Warrant BEFORE it runs; an action shape the checker cannot classify is refused or escalated to a human, never silently executed. The blast-radius problem of compiled scripts is answered head-on: a loop body is symbolically certified in-Warrant for ALL iterations before ANY iteration runs, and reversible effects execute in CoW transactions so a wrong-but-in-Warrant action costs a rollback, not a token-expensive re-derivation spiral; irreversible classes (send, purchase, external API) require an explicit Warrant grant or human escalation. Task correctness — not just safety — comes from deterministic acceptance predicates at joints: failing a joint re-opens a bounded hole seeded with the concrete failure evidence, which both raises reliability (errors caught at the joint, not at task end) and cuts cost (repair context is the evidence, not the history). Net effect on success rate is upward: the baseline agent's dominant failure modes — constraint amnesia, mid-task drift, silent bad side effects — are each intercepted by an artifact that is not the model grading itself.
designs.survivesCompaction: Trivially and by construction, because there is nothing load-bearing left in the context window to compact away. The Warrant, the Score, the execution ledger, and all checkpoint state live in the runtime store; each model call's context is RECONSTRUCTED from those artifacts (hole inputs + relevant Warrant clauses), so the enforced policy never depends on the transcript still containing it — the checker gates actions identically whether the session's history is intact, summarized, or gone. This is strictly stronger than compaction-robustness: if the orchestrating session dies entirely, the runtime resumes from the last certified joint with zero replayed context. The measured 0%→30-59% policy-violation-under-compaction failure cannot occur here, because the policy was never in the window in the first place — the window is a per-hole cache, not the source of truth.
designs.rareHardTaskMechanism: The payoff is a function of the ACTION vocabulary's structure and the TASK INSTANCE's internal repetitiveness — never of how often the task type has recurred — and the one thing that is amortized (the environment Warrant) amortizes over the WORKSPACE, which hosts unboundedly many never-before-seen tasks, not over task-type frequency. Concrete first-ever encounter: "migrate 200 config files across a breaking schema change without touching prod credentials." Call 1 explores 3 representative files (via a cheap sub-agent) and emits the Score — parse/transform/validate loop over the file list, holes declared for the 7 files that break the common pattern — plus a task Warrant narrowing writes to config/ and denying network. The checker proves the loop body in-Warrant once; 193 files transform for zero model tokens; 7 holes cost ~1K input tokens each; every write was gated pre-execution on a policy no compaction can drop. Per-instance counterfactual, no distribution needed: the execution ledger prices each compiled action at what its reactive equivalent would have cost (transcript-size-at-that-turn × prefill rate + an act call), and any single action can literally be replayed mechanism-off to validate the pricing — mechanism-on vs mechanism-off on THE SAME instance. Second or third repetition: the Score+Warrant pair IS the reusable skill, but it is retrieved and re-verified by the RUNTIME against the current Warrant, never injected into prompts — so reuse pays in output tokens without the catalog-injection input tax (the +9.7%/-net-negative trap). And on a genuinely one-off, fully observation-driven task, the design admits its floor: all-holes ≈ a plain reactive agent with fail-closed gating — safety yield at ~zero cost delta, never negative.
failureModes: Hole-granularity misjudgment: the planner compiles a stretch that was actually uncertain (overconfident determinism) — acceptance predicates catch it at the joint, but the repair costs a re-synthesis call; conversely an all-holes Score yields no savings (the floor). The triage estimator is itself fallible and occasionally burns one synthesis call on a task that turns out purely reactive.

Warrant authoring gap: an environment Warrant that is too broad is safety theater; one that is too narrow floods the human with escalations. The monotone-narrowing trick deliberately shifts the burden onto the standing policy's quality — that policy is now the single most security-critical artifact in the system and needs review discipline commensurate with that.

Closed-vocabulary poverty: real work eventually needs an unmodeled primitive (an interactive TUI, a CAPTCHA, a bespoke device). Fail-closed refusal is safe but stalls the task; the human-approved raw-action escape hatch that fixes the stall becomes the abused backdoor if it is made too convenient.

Symbolic-checker precision: abstract interpretation over shell text-manipulation is genuinely hard; over-approximation falsely blocks legitimate compiled loops, users fall back to per-action concrete checking, and the output savings shrink (safety intact, profit reduced). Under-approximation bugs in the checker are the catastrophic case and demand the checker be small, boring, and independently tested.

Minimal-context holes losing global coherence: a hole answered from its declared inputs alone can be locally right and globally wrong when the planner under-declared the dataflow; acceptance predicates are the backstop but only for properties someone thought to predicate — silent semantic drift that passes the tests is the residual risk.

Observation-driven tasks degrade the whole premise: where step N+1 genuinely depends on unpredictable output of step N (exploratory debugging, adversarial browsing), the Score degenerates and CONTINUO must honestly run as a gated reactive agent rather than pretend to compile — a system that pretends otherwise will ship broken Scores at machine speed.
roadmap: M1 — Gate first, save later: ship the closed action vocabulary + deterministic Warrant checker as a fail-closed proxy wrapped around an off-the-shelf reactive agent. No Score yet. Deliverable: compaction-proof pre-execution safety on real workloads, plus baseline per-turn cost telemetry that later milestones must beat. (Small team, weeks — the checker is deliberately boring code.)

M2 — The authority lattice: environment-Warrant language, model-proposed task narrowing with solver-checked subset relation, CoW transactional execution for reversible effect classes, and irreversibility-class escalation. Deliverable: model-authored specs admissible without self-certification.

M3 — The Score compiler and hole runtime: planner prompt → typed partial program; deterministic executor; minimal-context hole calls reconstructed from the store; the per-instance cost ledger that prices every compiled action against its reactive counterfactual (including single-action mechanism-off replay). Deliverable: first measured input+output savings on one instance of a never-seen task.

M4 — Symbolic loop certification + joints: abstract interpretation of loop bodies against the Warrant (one proof per stretch, per-action fallback), acceptance predicates at joints, bounded hole re-opening seeded with failure evidence. Deliverable: the 200-file class of task at O(holes) model calls with a pre-proved blast radius.

M5 — Disposable-transcript resumption and runtime-side reuse: resume any task from the last certified joint after total session loss; store Score+Warrant pairs and let the RUNTIME retrieve and re-verify them on repetition (zero prompt-injection tax); eval harness running mechanism-on/off on identical single instances across a suite of one-shot hard tasks. Deliverable: the rare-task claim demonstrated per-instance, not benchmark-averaged.

attacks: The flagship output-savings number is measured against the wrong baseline: a competently scaffolded agent already writes a script for a 50-item bulk job rather than repeating 50 manual turns, so the counterfactual '47 remaining items × observed per-item cost of the first 3' credits the compiler against a strawman a good prompt/tool-scaffold would never produce. This isn't a novelty nitpick — it invalidates the headline 97%/30-60% figures, which are illustrative arithmetic against an unrealistic baseline, not demonstrated savings against a competent one.

The anti-unification loop detector is the single most hand-waved component: no specified action representation (raw tool call? shell AST? diff structure?), no similarity threshold, no handling of data-dependent branching where item 37 legitimately needs different treatment. 'Detecting structurally isomorphic sequences' over heterogeneous shell/file/HTTP/browser actions at k=3 with real-world noise (flag order, whitespace, equivalent-but-differently-shaped calls) is a research problem dressed as a milestone (M4).

Fail-closed friction is worst exactly on the novel/rare tasks the design is pitched to save money on: an unclassifiable action shape always escalates, and novel tasks produce more unclassifiable shapes by definition. Each refusal round-trip (rejection message in, replanned action out) adds tokens nowhere counted in savesMagnitude. The design's own two headline claims — 'saves money on rare/hard tasks' and 'fails closed on novel shapes' — pull against each other and the tension is never reconciled or budgeted.

'Verified' is systematically oversold: the SMT proof only covers envelope-containment (safety), while the synthesized batch program's actual behavioral correctness rests on a single dry-run diff against item k+1, not a proof — a divergence that first appears at item 37 sails through. The design's own failureModes list ('Safe is not right') contradicts the correctnessMechanism section's claim that correctness 'is not regressed relative to baseline'; the two sections disagree and the rosier one is the headline.

Compaction-survival is proven only for the hard-constraint envelope, not for task correctness or mid-task emergent constraints. A verbal user instruction mid-task ('don't touch tenant X's config') that never gets promoted to the out-of-band envelope is exactly the kind of thing compaction erases, and the ledger/envelope machinery does nothing to protect it — the design's compaction claim answers a narrower question than the one it's presented as answering.

The Deed Ledger's own receipts are lossy compression of the same kind that caused the landmine being cited as motivation ('the same landmine moved earlier in the pipeline' — the design's own words). Mitigated by keeping raw observations addressable, but re-paging correctly depends on the agent's live judgment about when a receipt is insufficient — the same fallible judgment that caused the original failure, just relocated.

No mechanism for sub-agent/child-process composability: if the acting agent spawns a subagent (the harness this design targets routinely does), the child's action stream and the parent's within-instance ledger diverge — either every child is forced through the identical proxy with the identical envelope (raising the question of who ratifies a child-specific policy mid-task) or the k=3 detector is watching an incomplete stream and the guarantee has an unstated hole.

M2's validation milestone ('verify policy-violation rate stays at 0% under aggressive compaction') is close to unfalsifiable as specified: the gate sits at the tool boundary and doesn't consult the transcript, so it will trivially read 0% regardless of whether compaction destroyed task-relevant context — the metric validates the boundary-check design (already true by construction) rather than testing what actually degrades under compaction.

Net-dollar math elides real non-token infrastructure cost: SMT solving per mutating action, the ledger store, overlayfs/git-worktree checkpoint storage, and the synthesis-call routing are all real engineering/compute costs never weighed against the token savings — 'the token math closes' and 'the system is cheaper to run' are different claims and only the first is argued.

Checkpointed execution's core mechanism (overlayfs/git-worktree, staged outbox) only cleanly covers filesystem/git-scoped mutations; anything requiring a synchronous external side effect (login handshake, paginated purchase flow, an irreversible API call with no staging point) falls back to per-action human-gated flow, which caps savings precisely on the browser/API-heavy agentic workloads that are an increasingly large share of real usage — a scope limit the design admits but doesn't reflect in its top-line savings percentages.
crits.rareTaskVerdict: Partially real, not hand-waved but narrower than claimed. The within-instance compiler (k=3 structural-repetition trigger, per-instance counterfactual, corpus-free) is a genuine and distinctive mechanism for the subset of rare/hard tasks that have latent internal repetition (bulk renames, tree-wide transforms, scrape-and-transform) — this is the design's one real escape from the recurring-work niche, because the payoff is computed against this instance alone, no history needed. But it fails exactly the hardest cases within 'rare hard task': (a) genuinely singular, non-repetitive work (a one-shot debugging investigation, a novel architectural decision) gets nothing from the compiler and only the generic, well-worn checkpoint-retry fallback; (b) the anti-unification engine's operating representation and robustness to real-world action heterogeneity is unspecified, so its actual hit rate on truly rare tasks (which are rare partly because they're non-uniform) is unknown; (c) fail-closed escalation friction is structurally worst on novel task shapes, partially offsetting whatever the compiler saves. Net: one real, narrow, self-aware mechanism, oversold as covering the general case.
crits.compactionVerdict: Survives for the hard-constraint envelope by construction — the strongest, most concretely specified claim in the design, and it directly answers the cited landmine (policy falling out of a compacted summary) because enforcement never consults the transcript in the first place. Does not survive, and the prose blurs this, for task-level correctness: in-envelope is not the same as right, mid-task emergent constraints that never get formally promoted into the envelope have zero protection, and the Deed Ledger's own receipts are a second lossy-compression layer (admitted in the design's own failureModes) that can drop the caveat that mattered — the landmine relocated rather than defused.
crits.netTokenVerdict: Directionally well-engineered against the one trap the rubric names — no injected skill catalog, envelope and synthesized programs kept out-of-band, hash-stable prefix for caching — so on that specific axis the design does explicitly close the loop the naming-the-trap framing worries about. But 'does the math close' is answered with illustrative arithmetic (50 items × 800 tokens) rather than measured results, against a baseline (fully manual per-item repetition) that a competently scaffolded agent likely wouldn't run in the first place — which is the load-bearing flaw: if the real counterfactual is 'agent already writes a script,' the compiler's marginal token savings shrink to 'writes a *safety-verified* script instead of an unverified one,' a real but much smaller and differently-shaped benefit than the number implies. Additional uncounted costs: fail-closed escalation round-trips (worst on the very tasks targeted), and non-token infra cost (SMT solving, ledger store, checkpoint storage) that affects total cost even where tokens are saved. Verdict: plausible on input, overstated and wrong-baselined on output.
crits.buildability: Buildable in tiers, not as one project. M1 (proxy + envelope + fail-closed gate) is largely de-risked because the user's sibling project (openDaisugi) already runs this exact Z3-backed envelope/fail-closed architecture — but that's precisely the part that was already easy, and reuse buys nothing for the hard part. M2 (ledger + compaction) and M3 (checkpoint/rollback via overlayfs/git-worktree + stop-loss) are solid, well-understood engineering, buildable by a small team; M2's stated validation test ('policy-violation rate stays at 0% under compaction') is close to unfalsifiable as written since the gate never consults the transcript and will read 0% regardless of whether task-level correctness degraded — a milestone that looks like proof but isn't. M4 (the within-instance compiler: anti-unification + synthesis + dry-run verification) is the actual novel bet of the whole design and is scoped as a single milestone despite being closer to a research problem; its difficulty is understated relative to M1-M3. M5 is routine integration. The design degrades gracefully — M1/M2/M3/M5 alone form a shippable, valuable safety-and-compaction proxy even if M4 never lands — which is a genuine strength, but the roadmap doesn't flag M4 as the differently-risked milestone it is, and composability with sub-agent/multi-agent orchestration (routine in the harness this targets) is unaddressed: a spawned child's action stream diverges from the parent's ledger and the design has no stated answer for whose envelope governs or how the k=3 detector sees a complete stream.
crits.steelman: It correctly separates two things every other cost-reduction architecture conflates: put hard constraints and audit state OUTSIDE the context window so they survive compaction by construction rather than by hope, and amortize cost by watching for structure INSIDE a single task instance rather than betting on task recurrence — so both the safety guarantee and the savings mechanism are structural properties of the proxy, not emergent behaviors trusted to the acting model's memory or self-report.
keepIdeas: Externalize hard constraints and execution state to a proxy outside the context window, enforced at the tool boundary before the transcript is ever consulted — this is the one claim in the design that is compaction-proof by actual construction rather than by argument, and it stands on its own regardless of whether any other component works.
